items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: so I went to study with him and he heard it immediately

ctx.x: Well, when I came back from Brazil, I had a sort of breakdown where I lost all confidence and it was a mental thing perhaps and I went to a lot of different teachers and they all gave me the same old thing, you know, getting their individual selves into the act and trying to tell me the mistakes I had been making all these years, playing, but it wasn't helping me any, so I heard about Lennie Tristano and

I thought well, a blind man, he probably would hear something that nobody else heard, so I went to study with him and he heard it immediately. He said, 'Well, you are just all nerves, you are just closing up and not letting the sound ring through, no one else told me, with all the teachers I went to, and so he snapped me out of it and it was very interesting. I stayed with him for a very short period. We just went back to the basics of music. I didn't get into anything because I had to make a living going out on…
How nice, it was the sort of relationship that you established?
